India’s Renewable Energy Journey: Powering a Cleaner Future
articles.full_content:
India’s Energy Landscape
India’s renewable energy landscape is expanding rapidly to meet rising demand, strengthen energy security, and support a cleaner future. The transformation spans solar, wind, hydro, bio-energy, geothermal and green hydrogen.
Policy support, infrastructure development, domestic production, manufacturing expansion and wider energy access are shaping this transformation. From rooftop solar for households to large wind, floating solar and storage projects, India is steadily raising the share of renewables in its energy mix.
Numbers At a Glance:
• Total installed power capacity: Around 560 GW in October 2026, up from 249 GW in 2014.

• Non-fossil capacity: 308 GW as of 31 July 2026, accounting for 55% of total installed capacity.

• India ranks third globally in renewable energy installed capacity.

• India invested USD 63.7 billion in its renewable energy sector during July 2024–June 2026.

Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo (BRESE) 2026
Invest. Innovate. Inspire
The Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo (BRESE) 2026 was held from 2–5 November in New Delhi. The Summit brought together global policymakers, investors, industry leaders, manufacturers and innovators . Australia, Denmark, the European Union, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom participated as country partners. Thirteen Indian States and Union Territories, including Gujarat, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh, showcased their renewable energy potential, investment opportunities and manufacturing capabilities. The event also featured an exhibition bringing together 400+ manufacturers, technology providers, startups and research institutions. Discussions covered renewable energy financing, clean energy manufacturing, energy storage, emerging technologies and workforce development .
Solar Power: Scaling Up, Reaching More People
India’s installed solar capacity has reached ~175 GW (as of 31 October 2026), rising from 2.8 GW in 2014. Solar is now the largest component of India’s renewable energy capacity. India became the world’s second-largest solar growth market in 2025 , adding more than 37 GW of solar capacity, compared with 34 GW added by the United States.

articles.full_content:
Andhra Pradesh emerging as a major Renewable Energy Hub and India on Track for 500 GW Non-Fossil Capacity by 2030: Pralhad Joshi
Union Minister of Education, Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution and New & Renewable Energy, Shri Pralhad Joshi, addressed the session on “Securing the Sustainable Future: Energy Resilience, Clean Technologies, and Global Partnership” at the 31st CII Partnership Summit in Visakhapatnam today.
Referring to the MoUs exchanged at the summit, Shri Joshi noted that 17 Memoranda of Understanding and 3 Government Orders in the renewable energy sector represent investments worth ₹ 43,871 crore with an employment potential for around 4,700 people. He said these commitments demonstrate that India and Andhra Pradesh are “ walking the talk ” on clean energy and sustainable growth.
Highlighting India’s energy security progress, the Minister recalled that peak demand has risen from 123 GW in 2012 when a major grid collapse left North India in darkness for nearly 72 hours to 270 GW recently. This demand was met without interruption, with nearly 33% coming from non-fossil sources, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and Chief Minister Shri Chandrababu Naidu.
Shri Joshi underlined the importance of decentralized renewable energy saying that in Andhra Pradesh alone, 7.86 lakh households have been connected with rooftop solar. He added that, Nationally, under the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, 66 lakh households have already benefited, against an initial target of 1 crore. Installation pace has improved dramatically from 118 days for the first 1 lakh installations to an average of 6 days now, with the Ministry aiming for 5 days shortly. He noted that farmers and households are not only achieving zero electricity bills but also earning from excess power generation.
On the broader renewable energy journey, the Minister pointed out that solar capacity has grown from 2.8 GW in 2014 to 175 GW today. Non-fossil sources now account for about 55% of India’s total installed power capacity, putting the country firmly on track to achieve the 500 GW non-fossil capacity target by 2030. He reiterated Prime Minister Modi’s vision of “Zero Defect, Zero Effect” manufacturing and stressed that green energy will enable India to become a global green manufacturing hub.
Shri Joshi described India and Andhra Pradesh, under the leadership of Shri Narendra Modi and Shri Chandrababu Naidu an excellent and safe destination for investment due to political stability, policy consistency, and strong execution. He also referred to the upcoming PM-KUSUM 2, which will further solarize agricultural equipment and pumps.
Shri Joshi concluded by reiterating that India as a manufacturing hub will be powered by green energy giving our products a strong advantage in global markets.

articles.full_content:
National Highway Network in the State Doubled Since 2014; Greenfield Corridors, Expressways and Port Connectivity Projects to Slash Travel Times and Logistics Costs: Nitin Gadkari
13 November 2026
Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways, Shri Nitin Gadkari, today addressed the 31st Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) Summit in Visakhapatnam, outlining a transformative road infrastructure programme for Andhra Pradesh aligned with the vision of Viksit Bharat under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi.
Speaking on the theme of “Roads as the Foundation of Economic Growth”, he stressed that quality road infrastructure is essential for reducing logistics costs, attracting investment, generating jobs and driving prosperity.
Massive Scale of Development in Andhra Pradesh
Shri Gadkari informed that projects worth approximately ₹ 3 lakh crore are under implementation or planned in the state. Of these, projects costing ₹ 60,000 crore covering 4,750 km have already been completed; projects worth ₹ 1 lakh crore covering 2,500 km are ongoing; and upgrading works of ₹ 1.20 lakh crore covering 4,600 km are in progress. The national highway network in Andhra Pradesh has nearly doubled — from 4,100 km in 2014 to 8,700 km in 2026.
He highlighted three pillars for the state’s development:
• Greenfield Corridors, access-controlled Highways and Expressways
• Port connectivity
• Ring Roads and Bypasses.
These are being implemented in close consultation with the Government of Andhra Pradesh and are in line with the vision of Chief Minister Shri N. Chandrababu Naidu.
Key Greenfield Corridors and Expressways
• Bengaluru–Kadapa–Vijayawada Corridor (340 km, ₹ 14,000 crore): 70% complete; targeted for completion by December 2027. Expected to reduce distance by about 210 km and travel time from 12 hours to 4 hours, benefiting cement and mineral industries.
• Raipur–Visakhapatnam Corridor (460 km, ₹ 16,000 crore): 96% complete; completion targeted in 2027. Travel time to fall from 13 hours to 5 hours. The project will significantly enhance connectivity of Chhattisgarh and Odisha to Visakhapatnam Port (which supports 18-metre draft for large vessels) and passes through Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitarama Raju, Parvathipuram Manyam and Vizianagaram districts.
• Six-lining of Hyderabad–Vijayawada–Machilipatnam Highway (286 km, ₹ 12,000 crore): Public-Private Partnership Appraisal Committee approval obtained; awaiting Cabinet clearance. Expected to cut Hyderabad – Vijayawada travel time from 4.5 hours to 2.5 hours.
• Larger National corridors (including segments of Delhi–Mumbai Expressway extensions and north–south connectivity) will also benefit the state, reducing distances between northern and southern India by approximately 300 km in key stretches.
Port Connectivity and Ring Roads
Given Andhra Pradesh’s long coastline and major ports, the Minister emphasised the strategic importance of port-led development (building on the earlier Sagarmala initiative). Key

The focus is on empowering farmers to become agricultural entrepreneurs: PM
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today participated in the Kisan Tak Bharat Agriculture Conference 2026. Addressing the gathering on the occasion in the presence of agricultural scientists, agri-entrepreneurs, and farmers from across the nation, the Prime Minister commended the media group for its enthusiastic past participation in the cleanliness campaign and for dedicating two full days to organizing this innovative Kisan Mela.
Noting that the conference is taking place amid a festive atmosphere just days after Deepavali and during the ongoing Chhath Mahaparv, which is deeply rooted in agrarian life, the Prime Minister pointed out that major Indian festivals such as Bihu, Pongal, Onam, Baisakhi, Sarhul, and Pola are intrinsically tied to farming. “Meaning, agriculture and farming are our culture, our tradition, and the foundation of our social life,” observed PM Modi.
Recalling his Red Fort address on the seven streams of national strength (Saptadhara) required for a Viksit Bharat, in which agriculture serves as a primary pillar, the Prime Minister emphasized that the significance of such farmer conferences has grown manifold because national development depends directly on agricultural modernization. “The building of a Viksit Bharat is simply not possible without developing agriculture, without making farming smarter, and without empowering the farmer,” asserted Shri Modi.
Illustrating the close link between agricultural growth and national progress through a widely discussed World Bank study showing that 50 crore Indians escaped poverty in just 12 to 13 years with a sharp decline in rural poverty among small farmers and farm laborers, the Prime Minister highlighted that this period coincided with India's agriculture sector achieving an average growth rate above 4 percent for the first decade since independence.
Observing that farmers and agricultural experts understand the necessity of continuous policy and methodological evolution, the Prime Minister pointed out that as global markets, dietary habits, weather patterns, and technologies evolved over time, farmers needed to be empowered afresh. “Merely filling the granaries of food grains is not enough,” asserted Shri Modi.

articles.title: English rendering of PM's address at the Kisan Tak Bharat Agriculture Conference
articles.full_content:
You also have my heartfelt greetings on this sacred festival of Diwali, and with the programme of Chhathi Maiya also approaching, I extend my very best wishes for that as well. My greetings to all of you.
Chairman and Editor-in-Chief of the India Today Group, Shri Arun Puri ji, the agricultural scientists, agri-entrepreneurs, farmer friends, and all distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen who have come from across the country for this programme.
First of all, I wholeheartedly congratulate the India Today Group for this innovative initiative. When the country launched the cleanliness campaign, the India Today Group participated in it very enthusiastically. Now you have organised this Kisan Mela, and dedicated two full days to it. This is a very positive beginning. I congratulate all of you. And Arun ji speaks such excellent Hindi, so double congratulations for that.
This event is taking place at a time when the country is in a festive mood. Two or three days ago, we celebrated the festival of Diwali, and now the spirit of the Chhath Mahaparva is all around us. The festival of Chhath is deeply connected with agricultural life, and in our country, most festivals are linked with farming and agriculture. Bihu, Pongal, Onam, Baisakhi, Sarhul, Pola, many such festivals are connected with agriculture. In other words, farming is our culture, our tradition, and the foundation of our social life.
From the Red Fort, I had spoken about the seven streams of strength for a Viksit India, and among these, agriculture is a principal stream. Building a Viksit India is simply not possible without developing agriculture, without making farming smarter, and without empowering farmers. That is why the importance of such farmer conferences becomes even greater.
You can understand the relationship between farming and the country's progress through two important facts. Recently, a World Bank study on poverty was released, and it is being discussed across the world. It states that within just 12–13 years, 50 crore poor people in India have defeated poverty. It also states that poverty has declined very rapidly in villages. This means that a large number of small farmers and agricultural labourers have overcome poverty. Now look at the coincidence. During the past decade, India's agricultural growth rate has remained above 4 percent. This is the first decade after Independence in which the country's agriculture sector has achieved an average growth rate of more than 4 percent, for the first time since Independence. And during this same period, a large number of poor people in villages have defeated poverty. But unfortunately, people trapped in angles and agendas of news coverage fail to notice this achievement of the country.

NITI Aayog Launches Report on “Impact Assessment of PLI Schemes”
articles.full_content:
NITI Aayog today released the report titled “Impact Assessment of PLI Schemes”, prepared in collaboration with the Indian Institute of Management, Ahmedabad as the knowledge partner. The report recognizes the PLI Scheme as a flagship policy intervention launched by the Government of India to enhance India’s manufacturing competitiveness, integrate Indian firms into global value chains, and accelerate the journey towards an Atmanirbhar Bharat. By providing production-linked incentives to a select set of high-performing firms, the scheme is designed to be self-sustaining, encouraging adoption of advanced technologies, capacity creation, and sustained growth in output and exports.
Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes, implemented by various Ministries and Departments, have emerged as a successful initiative for scaling up domestic manufacturing, investment and production, while strengthening India’s position in global value chains by driving exports, building domestic capabilities and enhancing competitiveness. Acting as a catalyst for industrial deepening, employment and export expansion, the initiative is advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 through a globally competitive manufacturing sector.
The report presents a sector-wise assessment of the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme across all 14 sectors notified by the Government of India, examining its impact on the key parameters of investment, additional production, exports, and employment generation. The assessment is based on sector-wise collection of firm-level data shared by implementing Ministries, supplemented by industry-level inputs from authenticated sources. Sectoral outcomes have been categorized into four broad groups: On-Track, Partial Impact, Insignificant Evidence of Impact, and Data unavailable; providing a structured and comparative overview of the scheme’s progress across sectors.
The report finds that sectors with strong industry participation have demonstrated encouraging outcomes under the scheme. Pharmaceuticals, Mobile Manufacturing under Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing (LSEM), Food Processing, Telecom, White Goods, Automobiles and Drones have shown notable progress in investment, production and capacity creation, with the Drones sector emerging as an early implementation success.
Manufacturing capacity in High Efficiency Solar PV Modules has also expanded significantly, reflecting growing domestic capability and strengthening India’s renewable energy manufacturing ecosystem. The report further notes that sectors involving advanced and emerging technologies such as ACC Batteries, Specialty Steel and Technical Textiles are witnessing gradual capacity creation and ecosystem development, which are expected to contribute significantly to India’s long-term industrial growth trajectory. Across sectors, the scheme has played an important role in stimulating investment, enhancing manufacturing capacity and strengthening industrial competitiveness.
